_comment: The golden correctness harness. Every question carries hand-reviewed reference SQL over the jaffle-golden seed (dev.* marts of the real jaffle-shop-duckdb project, 12 customers). At test time the reference SQL is executed against the same seeded engine the server queries, and the run's result rows must equal it. `columns` maps each reference column to the names the product may legitimately use for it. `ordered` means row order is part of the answer. `tier` is the trust the answer must carry. `outcome` is 'rows' unless a clarification or an honest gap is the correct answer. Identity rule: rankings of customers/products are keyed by their id and display the name; a result may carry the id, the name, or both, and matches the reference through either.

questions.question: who are the top customers for beverage product category
questions.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, SUM(CASE WHEN oi.is_drink_item THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS drink_revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY drink_revenue DESC LIMIT 10
questions.note: Certified first: the top_beverage_customers block, served as published, is the governed answer (it groups by customer name; the caveat that two customers sharing a name would merge is recorded on the answer). A keyed AI-written answer with the name beside the id is also accepted.

questions.question: who are the top customers
questions.sql: SELECT customer_id, customer_name, lifetime_spend FROM dev.customers ORDER BY lifetime_spend DESC LIMIT 10
questions.note: Lifetime spend including tax is the customers mart definition; pretax spend is an acceptable reading (the Revenue term's own rule names pretax product revenue) and is an alternative with its own values. "Top customers" names no measure; the certified customer_profile ordering (lifetime spend) or the lifetime_spend metric are governed readings, and one bounded clarification between gross and pretax spend is also correct.

alternatives.sql: SELECT customer_id, customer_name, lifetime_spend_pretax AS lifetime_spend FROM dev.customers ORDER BY lifetime_spend_pretax DESC LIMIT 10

questions.question: top 5 customers by revenue
questions.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, SUM(oi.product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

alternatives.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, SUM(o.order_total) AS order_total FROM dev.orders o JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY order_total DESC LIMIT 5

questions.note: The governed Revenue term admits gross order revenue (order_total) as well as pretax product revenue; both readings are accepted.

questions.question: total revenue
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items
questions.note: The governed Revenue term defines BOTH gross order revenue (orders.order_total, incl. tax) and product revenue (order_items.product_price, pretax). Either governed reading, or one bounded clarification between them, is correct; a silent third definition is not.

alternatives.sql: SELECT SUM(order_total) AS revenue FROM dev.orders

questions.question: revenue by month

questions.note: The certified monthly_revenue block sums order_total (incl. tax); the semantic revenue metric sums product_price. Either is a governed monthly revenue answer; the harness accepts the one whose label matches and checks its numbers against that definition.

alternatives.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', ordered_at) AS month, SUM(order_total) AS gross_revenue FROM dev.orders GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

alternatives.sql: SELECT SUM(o.order_total) AS revenue FROM dev.orders o JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.customer_name = 'Ryan Byrd'
SELECT SUM(lifetime_spend) AS lifetime_spend FROM dev.customers WHERE customer_name = 'Ryan Byrd'

questions.note: Two measures of the same customer, one filter matched case-insensitively. 'Total revenue' may follow either governed reading of the Revenue term (order total incl. tax, or pretax product revenue); the beverage restriction applies only to the beverage measure.

alternatives.sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(o.order_total) FROM dev.orders o JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE lower(c.customer_name)='ryan byrd') AS revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN oi.is_drink_item THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS drink_revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE lower(c.customer_name) = 'ryan byrd'

questions.question: what was the average order value in 2025
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(oi.product_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS average_order_value FROM dev.order_items oi WHERE oi.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2026-01-01'

alternatives.sql: SELECT SUM(o.order_total) / COUNT(o.order_id) AS average_order_value FROM dev.orders o WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-01-01'
SELECT SUM(o.subtotal) / COUNT(o.order_id) AS average_order_value FROM dev.orders o WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-01-01'

questions.note: A period average is revenue over orders IN THAT PERIOD: a derived ratio of two governed measures sharing the order-date time role, disclosed as such. The dbt metric average_order_value (lifetime_spend_pretax / count_lifetime_orders at the customers grain, over first_ordered_at) is a cohort average and is NOT the answer to 'in 2025'.

questions.question: what is the average order value of customers first acquired in 2024
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(c.lifetime_spend_pretax) / SUM(c.count_lifetime_orders) AS average_order_value FROM dev.customers c WHERE c.first_ordered_at >= '2024-01-01' AND c.first_ordered_at < '2025-01-01'

alternatives.sql: SELECT SUM(oi.product_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS average_order_value FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.first_ordered_at >= '2024-01-01' AND c.first_ordered_at < '2025-01-01'

SELECT SUM(o.order_total) / COUNT(o.order_id) AS average_order_value FROM dev.orders o JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.first_ordered_at >= '2024-01-01' AND c.first_ordered_at < '2025-01-01'

questions.note: The question names the cohort axis itself (first acquired in 2024): the governed customer-grain metric restricted by first_ordered_at, or the cohort's revenue per order, or one bounded clarification between them. The axis is explicit, so the window is never applied silently on a different time role. The seed's twelve customers all first ordered in 2024.

questions.question: What was our gross profit in 2025, and our gross margin percentage?
questions.sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(oi.product_price) FROM dev.order_items oi WHERE oi.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2026-01-01') - (SELECT SUM(o.order_cost) FROM dev.orders o WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-01-01') AS gross_profit, ((SELECT SUM(oi.product_price) FROM dev.order_items oi WHERE oi.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2026-01-01') - (SELECT SUM(o.order_cost) FROM dev.orders o WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-01-01')) * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(oi.product_price) FROM dev.order_items oi WHERE oi.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2026-01-01') AS gross_margin
questions.note: order_gross_profit is a derived metric (revenue - order_cost) whose inputs live on two relations; the relational tier aggregates each on its own island and evaluates the formula, the margin is a disclosed ratio. On MetricFlow the same intent compiles with a metric_time window.

alternatives.sql: SELECT gross_profit, gross_margin * 100 AS gross_margin FROM (SELECT (SELECT SUM(oi.product_price) FROM dev.order_items oi WHERE oi.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2026-01-01') - (SELECT SUM(o.order_cost) FROM dev.orders o WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-01-01') AS gross_profit, ((SELECT SUM(oi.product_price) FROM dev.order_items oi WHERE oi.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2026-01-01') - (SELECT SUM(o.order_cost) FROM dev.orders o WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-01-01')) * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(oi.product_price) FROM dev.order_items oi WHERE oi.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2026-01-01') AS gross_margin)
alternatives.note: AI-written SQL may give the margin in percentage points (79.6) instead of a fraction (0.796); both are accepted, as for growth-jul-aug.

questions.question: Compare August with July 2025 sales before tax and show the percentage growth.
questions.note: A month-over-month comparison the semantic engine cannot express as an offset metric is still answerable as two scoped measures and the change between them: the two totals plus the growth as a fraction of July. A silently zero growth, or two totals with the growth only in the prose, is the failure this case guards against. AI-written SQL may give the growth in percentage points (8.06) instead of a fraction (0.0806); both are accepted.
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN oi.ordered_at >= '2025-07-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2025-08-01' THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_july, SUM(CASE WHEN oi.ordered_at >= '2025-08-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2025-09-01' THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_august, (SUM(CASE WHEN oi.ordered_at >= '2025-08-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2025-09-01' THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) * 1.0  - SUM(CASE WHEN oi.ordered_at >= '2025-07-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2025-08-01' THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END)) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN oi.ordered_at >= '2025-07-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2025-08-01' THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) * 1.0, 0) AS growth FROM dev.order_items oi

alternatives.sql: SELECT revenue_july, revenue_august, growth * 100 AS growth FROM (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN oi.ordered_at >= '2025-07-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2025-08-01' THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_july, SUM(CASE WHEN oi.ordered_at >= '2025-08-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2025-09-01' THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_august, (SUM(CASE WHEN oi.ordered_at >= '2025-08-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2025-09-01' THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) * 1.0  - SUM(CASE WHEN oi.ordered_at >= '2025-07-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2025-08-01' THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END)) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN oi.ordered_at >= '2025-07-01' AND oi.ordered_at < '2025-08-01' THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) * 1.0, 0) AS growth FROM dev.order_items oi)

questions.question: How much revenue do we have?
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items
questions.note: The name wins: unqualified 'revenue' is the metric named revenue (pretax product revenue). order_total (including tax) is accepted only when the question qualifies it. Deterministic after interpretation; the provenance says 'governed default: the question names the metric revenue'.

questions.question: How much revenue do we have including tax?
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(order_total) AS order_total FROM dev.orders
questions.note: 'including tax' is a qualifier: the gross order total stays.

questions.question: How much revenue comes from new versus returning customers?
questions.sql: SELECT c.customer_type, SUM(oi.product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_type
questions.note: Pretax revenue split between new and returning customers. Two governed readings: by the customer_type dimension (new = only the first order placed, returning = ordered more than once; the answer defines the type from the dbt column description), or per order by customer_order_number (the first order versus later ones; the reading line states it). Gross order_total is not accepted: the question says revenue.

alternatives.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN o.customer_order_number = 1 THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS new_customer_revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN o.customer_order_number <> 1 THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS returning_customer_revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id

questions.question: Why is our revenue down by region, and which region should we invest in?
questions.note: Region is not modeled and 'why'/'invest' ask for an explanation and a decision Ask does not compute: a named gap with zero SQL and the answerable reading (revenue) stated. Never the adjacent certified monthly trend.

questions.question: revenue by shopper
questions.sql: SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(oi.product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.customer_id ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note: "Shopper" is a business concept known under two keys (the customer record, and the customer on each order). A concept is discovery and clarification, never an executable identity (A-005): the expected turn asks which binding to use; a reading that resolves to the customer record on its own is also accepted.
